chunks: And he (peace be upon him) said:
Contentment is wealth that does not diminish.

key_terms.الْقَنَاعَةُ: Contentment, satisfaction with what one has
key_terms.لَا يَنْفَدُ: That does not diminish or run out

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic definition of true wealth?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) defines contentment (qana'ah) as a form of wealth that is inexhaustible, contrasting it with material possessions which are subject to loss and depletion. In Shia scholarly tradition, this hadith underscores the concept of inner sufficiency, where the soul's satisfaction with divine decree becomes a permanent asset that outlasts temporal riches. This teaching encourages believers to cultivate spiritual resilience by valuing internal peace over external accumulation.

en.sayed-ali-raza: 57. Amīr al-mu’minīn, peace be upon him, said:
Contentment is wealth that does not diminish. [1]
